title: Field fabric: synthesis and minifeature proposals
body:
Purpose: quick synthesis of recent field feedback (~20 customer threads, 6 NPS follow-ups) and a compact set of low-risk minifeature proposals we can prototype in <6 weeks. This doc is intentionally terse: highlight problems with examples, propose focused patches, call out open questions for eng/product.

Methodology: pulled threads from support inbox and CS weekly notes (2026-07-01..2026-07-31), prioritized by frequency and operational pain (latency incidents, billing surprises, onboarding friction). Clustered feedback into thematic problems, validated with one follow-up call per major account when unclear.

Executive summary (1 paragraph): Customers repeatedly signal three types of friction: intermittent latency spikes during long-turn conversations, surprising cost blowups on high-throughput reranking/embeddings workloads, and onboarding gaps for Private deployments (network & KMS steps). There are multiple low-effort patches that would reduce operational noise and provide measurable CX wins: a per-route cost budget warning, a KV-cache health indicator and auto-warm hint, a reduced-privilege onboarding checklist for Private, and a small UI affordance to visualize model-variant fallbacks.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We have a few calls per week where latency jumps from 80ms to 1.3s mid-conversation — it kills interactive demos. We can’t tell if it’s batching, GC, or model swap." — large SaaS POC
- "Our embeddings bill doubled after switching to batch size 64; we didn’t get a heads-up that cost/unit would change." — growth-stage startup
- "Private install was straightforward until KMS. The KMS guide assumes a previous HSM config; our infra team had to open a ticket." — regulated customer

Clusters and notes: 
1) Latency spike visibility (high frequency, medium severity)
- Symptoms: sudden p90->p99 divergence during multi-turn chat or when reranking with long contexts.
- Root-cause hypotheses from threads: transient kernel fallback (GPU->CPU), KV cache misses during shard rebalancing, per-request heavy preprocessing.
- Current friction: customers open tickets; SREs must correlate traces across models and infra.
- Short-term patch (minifeature A): 
  Name: KV-cache health and prewarm hint
  What: add an indicator on route dashboard showing KV cache hit-rate and last warm timestamp; expose a simple API /admin/prewarm?route=xxx that triggers async prewarm.
  Expected customer impact: reduces unexplained mid-chat latency for 40% of reported incidents.
  Estimated complexity: S (front-end dashboard + one small server endpoint + metric instrument).
  Owners suggested: eng-observability + serving-runtime (collab).
  Risks: minor performance overhead when computing hit-rate; can be throttled.

2) Cost surprises on batching/embeddings (medium frequency, high business sensitivity)
- Symptoms: customers change batch/parallel settings and see non-linear cost increases.
- Friction: lack of upfront per-route cost simulation or quick sanity check.
- Short-term patch (minifeature B): 
  Name: per-route cost preview and soft budget alerts
  What: when changing batch/parallel/quantization for a route, surface a preview that estimates cost delta (30/90/360 day) based on recent traffic and a toggle to enable a soft budget that emits warnings (dashboard + webhook) before billing threshold.
  Expected customer impact: reduces surprise billing tickets and supports self-serve tuning.
  Estimated complexity: M (needs traffic sampling + simple estimator + UI + webhook plumbing).
  Owners suggested: product-hosted-api + billing infra.
  Quick UX note: default to "estimate conservative (10% overhead)" and show best/worst case.

3) Private deployment onboarding friction (lower frequency, high severity)
- Symptoms: network/KMS steps cause multi-day stalls; tickets escalate to sales.
- Friction: docs are fragmented; checklist assumes specific cloud setups.
- Short-term patch (minifeature C): 
  Name: Private quickstart minimal checklist + role-scoped templates
  What: produce a condensed step-by-step quickstart for infra and another for security (KMS templates, HSM optional path), plus provide terraform snippets for common clouds. Add a "preflight validator" script customers can run that emits warnings for missing ports, DNS, and KMS policy gaps.
  Expected customer impact: reduce time-to-first-inference for Private by ~30% and cut triage time for CS by half.
  Estimated complexity: M (doc + small validator script + templates).
  Owners suggested: solutions-engineering + product-private-deployments.

4) Model-variant transparency & graceful fallback visualization (medium frequency, medium severity)
- Symptoms: apps unexpectedly get served a smaller/faster model during capacity fallback and product teams are unaware.
- Friction: lack of visibility causes QA regressions and surprise quality deltas.
- Short-term patch (minifeature D): 
  Name: per-request variant trail + fallback timeline
  What: add lightweight logging visible in the route trace showing which model variant served the request and whether fallback triggered; provide a visualization that shows when fallbacks happened in the last 7/30 days correlated with error/latency spikes.
  Expected customer impact: faster root-cause for quality regressions, easier audit for enterprise customers.
  Estimated complexity: M (instrumentation + trace UI).
  Owners suggested: console-and-rollouts + serving-runtime.

5) Low-friction canary rollback trigger (low effort, high impact for rollouts)
- Symptoms: canary flags show quality regression but rolling back requires manual steps and coordination.
- Short-term patch (minifeature E): 
  Name: one-click canary rollback button (soft)
  What: add a console action to revert canary routing to previous variant and optionally create a rollback incident in the team’s tracker (pre-filled template). Implement as a guarded operation with confirmation and automatic monitoring for 1 hour after revert.
  Expected customer impact: reduce MTTR for bad rollouts and increase confidence in canary experiments.
  Estimated complexity: S (console change + small orchestration hook).
  Owners suggested: product-console + platform-engineering.

Cross-cutting operational asks (not full features):
- Better incident annotation flow: allow CS to tag traces with ticket ids and a quick note so SREs can search. Low-effort.
- More explicit guidance on quantization trade-offs: a short one-pager linked from the model catalog showing quality vs. cost examples for common workloads.

Prioritization sketch (rough):
- Minifeature A (KV prewarm hint): P0
- Minifeature B (cost preview + soft budget): P0/P1 (high customer sensitivity)
- Minifeature C (Private quickstart + preflight): P1
- Minifeature D (variant trail): P1
- Minifeature E (canary rollback button): P2 (low effort, nice to have)

Open questions for product/eng: 
- For cost preview estimator, do we prefer a purely sample-based approach or a lightweight simulator that extrapolates token-level compute? Trade-offs: simulator is more accurate but requires model profiles.
- For KV prewarm: do we expose prewarm to customers or keep it admin-only? Suggestion: admin-only + opt-in for enterprise.
- For preflight validator: what scope of checks do we want initially to avoid false positives (ports, DNS, KMS policies only)?

Next steps (concrete):
- CS to sync with product-hosted-api + observability next Thu (2026-08-12) to align acceptance criteria for A and B.
- Engineering triage to size A/B/C/D in 2-week cadence; propose small spike for cost estimator.
- Create a one-pager for sales enablement summarizing Private quickstart improvements.

Appendix: short mapping of threads (anonymized ids) to clusters - used for traceability: THREAD-842, THREAD-859, THREAD-863, THREAD-871, THREAD-910, THREAD-922, THREAD-934. Follow-ups assigned: Maya (lead), Diego (eng liaison), Priya (solutions).

Notes to self: keep proposals intentionally narrow. Avoid spec creep. If A or B require >6 wks, re-evaluate scope to split into smaller deployables.

End of doc.
